{"author": null, "closed_at": null, "collaborating_teams": null, "collaborating_users": null, "created_at": null, "credits": [{"login": "Paincakess", "type": "reporter"}], "credits_detailed": [{"state": "accepted", "type": "reporter", "user": {"avatar_url": "https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/78134328?v=4", "events_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/events{/privacy}", "followers_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/followers", "following_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/following{/other_user}", "gists_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/gists{/gist_id}", "gravatar_id": "", "html_url": "https://github.com/Paincakess", "id": 78134328, "login": "Paincakess", "node_id": "MDQ6VXNlcjc4MTM0MzI4", "organizations_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/orgs", "received_events_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/received_events", "repos_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/repos", "site_admin": false, "starred_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/starred{/owner}{/repo}", "subscriptions_url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess/subscriptions", "type": "User", "url": "https://api.github.com/users/Paincakess", "user_view_type": "public"}}], "cve_id": null, "cvss": {"score": 5.3, "vector_string": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N"}, "cvss_severities": {"cvss_v3": {"score": 5.3, "vector_string": "CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N"}, "cvss_v4": {"score": null, "vector_string": null}}, "cwe_ids": ["CWE-696", "CWE-862"], "cwes": [{"cwe_id": "CWE-696", "name": "Incorrect Behavior Order"}, {"cwe_id": "CWE-862", "name": "Missing Authorization"}], "description": "## Summary

The `POST /settings/owner` endpoint derives its authorization from the settings singleton write it performs, which
passes through the permission layer. In affected versions two side effects ran before that write: an outbound owner
report to the configured compliance intake endpoint containing request-supplied fields, and, if that report failed, a
direct database write setting `directus_settings.project_status` to `pending`. Directus populates accountability
globally but does not reject unauthenticated requests at the middleware layer, so an unauthenticated caller received
`403 Forbidden` while both side effects had already been dispatched.

## Details

The route has no per-route authorization guard. The outbound report was issued ahead of the settings write and was
intentionally not awaited, so it continued to settle after the outer request had already failed with a permission error.

The report is a POST to the configured compliance endpoint (`COMPLIANCE_URL`, default `compliance.directus.io`) whose
body is assembled from the request payload (`project_owner`, `org_name`, `project_usage`, `product_updates`) together
with the instance's `project_id` and version. Every payload field is caller-supplied and none are validated before the
report is sent. The destination is fixed by configuration and is not influenced by the request.

The rejection handler attached to that call performed a direct query-builder update of
`directus_settings.project_status`, bypassing the permission layer entirely. This path is reached only when the outbound
report fails, which is the standing condition on deployments with restricted outbound network access.
`project_status = 'pending'` is the flag read by the daily project status job, which re-sends the stored owner
information and then clears the flag.

An unauthenticated read of `project_id` from the settings table also preceded the check. That value is not returned to
the caller and is not disclosed.

Both side effects require `PROJECT_OWNER_ENABLED`, which is enabled by default. With it disabled the reporting helper
returns before issuing any request, and neither side effect occurs.

## Impact

An unauthenticated caller able to reach the API could:

- Cause the instance to submit caller-controlled strings to the configured compliance intake endpoint, from the
  instance's own network position and under its `project_id`, with no authorization. This permits submitting spurious
  owner records attributable to the deployment and polluting the intake pipeline.
- On deployments where the outbound report fails, set `directus_settings.project_status` to `pending`. The written value
  is fixed and not attacker-chosen. Its effect is that the daily project status job sends one additional owner report
  per day until a report succeeds.

The stored owner information itself is not modified, nothing is disclosed to the caller, and no privilege escalation or
access to other collections follows. The persistent effect on the instance is limited to a single non-security settings
field.

## Workarounds

For deployments that cannot upgrade immediately:

- Set `PROJECT_OWNER_ENABLED=false` if the project owner and compliance reporting flow is not in use. Neither side
  effect can be triggered while it is disabled.
- Block `POST /settings/owner` at a reverse proxy in front of Directus, or restrict it to authenticated requests.
- If the flag has already been flipped, clearing `directus_settings.project_status` returns the instance to its prior
  state.

## Credit

Reported by @Paincakess
